svg.text: piScanner wiring — Raspberry Pi 5, board viewed from above
40-pin header: pin 1 is the square pad at the end farthest from the USB/Ethernet ports. Odd pins = inner row, even pins = board-edge row.
Optional 3.5" SPI display HAT covers pins 1–26
USB-C cable: powers the Pi + Pi types barcodes as a keyboard
Never connect 5 V to a GPIO pin.
A 3.5" SPI display HAT covers pins 1–26;
a magnetic (coil) buzzer needs an NPN
transistor. Installer enables PWM on GPIO12.
trigger and beeper sit on the free pins.
Trigger uses the Pi's internal pull-up;
A PC port may not power Pi 5 + Brio.
If it browns out, use a USB-C power/
data splitter with a 5 V 5 A supply.
